answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed when two identities are proven to share one operator. This turns cheap duplication into a real cost: a hollow fleet of sock puppets cannot whisper its way past the bond, because each copy must lock funds that are forfeited on detection. Honest agents keep a crystal-clear, auditable record of their stake and past trades, so peers can price trust from verifiable history rather than from how many voices claim it.
